artists.biography: Inspired by Janis Joplin , Rival Sons and Hozier, Children of the Sün embody both the carefree and reflective sides of classic rock music with folk-vibes. Following their 2018 success in the Swedish music competition Livekarusellen, the band released a self-titled EP and later came under the wing of The Sign Records, joining acts such as Hällas ,MaidaVale , Skraeckoedlan, and The Hawkins . In 2019 the band released their first full-length album which was received with great love from the audience and the vinyl sold out just a few months after the release. They´re now back with their sophomore album "Roots". A album that shows depth and growth to the bands sound. Read more on Last.fm. Children of the Sün.biography: Inspired by Janis Joplin , Rival Sons and Hozier, Children of the Sün embody both the carefree and reflective sides of classic rock music with folk-vibes. Following their 2018 success in the Swedish music competition Livekarusellen, the band released a self-titled EP and later came under the wing of The Sign Records, joining acts such as Hällas ,MaidaVale , Skraeckoedlan, and The Hawkins . In 2019 the band released their first full-length album which was received with great love from the audience and the vinyl sold out just a few months after the release. They´re now back with their sophomore album "Roots". A album that shows depth and growth to the bands sound. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Children of the Sün's 2022 album Roots is a vibrant exploration of retro rock, blending elements of psychedelic rock, blues, pop, and gospel into a cohesive and atmospheric sound. Released through The Sign Records, the album follows their well-received 2019 debut Flowers, marking a progression in both songwriting depth and musical maturity. The band’s signature style is defined by multi-layered vocal harmonies, expressive melodies, and a dynamic rhythm section, often shifting between acoustic intimacy and full-band grooves. Tracks like “Blood Boils Hot,” “Eden,” and “In Silva” showcase their ability to balance melancholy with energy, creating a rich sonic landscape that evokes the spirit of late 1960s rock while remaining distinctly contemporary.

Roots was met with strong critical acclaim, praised for its authenticity, emotional resonance, and genre-blending approach. Reviewers highlighted the album’s ability to capture the essence of classic rock and psychedelic sounds without feeling derivative, noting its thoughtful lyrics and immersive production. The album solidified Children of the Sün’s reputation as leading figures in the modern retro rock scene, earning a 9/10 rating from Apocalypse Later Music Reviews and positive coverage across several music publications. As their second full-length release, Roots stands as a significant milestone in the band’s discography, reflecting both their artistic growth and their commitment to the genre’s timeless appeal.
